title: Fairness after a domestic custom changes
meaning: A changed domestic custom offers support more easily when its ending need not wait for a final audit of all earlier concessions.
text: Home may rest on customs in which you recognise shared life: spending weekends, preparing evenings and providing essentials. The Hierophant in the physical position of Muladhara describes these repeated actions. Justice in energy tests your footing through strict accounting of concessions: what each has already done and whose turn it is to change the familiar. Death in emotions experiences the ending of an old domestic form. Needed change may therefore be delayed not through misunderstanding but through wanting the entire cost of past participation balanced first.

For example, the customary Saturday grocery trip no longer fits your schedules. Discussing a replacement repeatedly returns to who previously accepted inconvenient timing more often. **An old form can end without a perfect settlement of the entire past.** Recognising earlier efforts matters, but need not hold this week inside a habit that no longer works. A new agreement can answer today’s need while respecting what once sustained two people.

The difficulty is hearing another routine as an attempt to forget invested work. Change appears unfair before beginning, so you keep doing the inconvenient thing out of loyalty to the past. Home loses flexibility. Stability grows through acknowledging an old custom’s cost and ending its form without asking the future to repay every distant concession. Earlier care can retain value even when its arrangement has finished.
